---
title: Receive webhooks
description: Register a webhook, check that each webhook delivery came from your instance, and handle repeated, out-of-order and failed webhook deliveries.
job: A builder registers a webhook, checks each delivery came from the instance, and handles repeats, order and failures.
---

A webhook lets a service react to changes without holding a connection open: you register a URL, and Marfa posts each event you chose to it. [Events](/build/events) says when to use one rather than the [event stream](/build/keep-in-sync).

The receiving service needs a key that holds `webhooks.manage` and reads the types its webhook is told about ([Manage keys](/use/manage-keys)). **A webhook belongs to the key or app that registered it**, and Marfa sends it nothing once that key expires, is revoked or loses `webhooks.manage`. A key that holds `keys.manage`, such as the owner's, can also see and delete any webhook.

## Register a webhook

[Create a webhook](/reference/api/webhooks/createWebhook) takes the `url` to post to and the `events` you want, each named from the Catalog's [Events](/catalog/events), with no wildcard. `type_filter` limits item events to one type and its subtypes:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa webhooks create --delivery-url https://example.com/marfa \
  --event item.created --event item.updated --type-filter core.note
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /webhooks
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://example.com/marfa",
  "events": ["item.created", "item.updated"],
  "type_filter": "core.note"
}
```

Marfa answers with the webhook and its `secret`, **shown only once**, which signs each delivery; to choose your own, send one of at least 32 characters. It receives only events written after you register it. A `url` that isn't public is refused unless the owner turns on the `allow_private_addresses` [setting](/run/settings).

## Check each webhook delivery

A delivery is a `POST` whose body is the event as the stream sends it, plus `event_id`, `delivered_at` and a `delivery_id` that is the same on every attempt. Anyone can post to your URL, so check `X-Marfa-Signature` first: it reads `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is the HMAC-SHA-256, under your webhook's secret, of `t`, a period and the raw body. **Compute it over the bytes exactly as they arrived:** parsing the JSON again changes them. This check refuses a signature more than five minutes old; a repeat inside that window still verifies, so the table below is keyed by `delivery_id`:

```ts title="verify-signature.mts"
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifySignature(rawBody: Buffer, header: string | undefined, secret: string, toleranceSeconds = 300): boolean {
  const fields = new Map((header ?? "").split(",").map((part) => part.trim().split("=") as [string, string]));
  const t = fields.get("t");
  const v1 = fields.get("v1");
  if (!t || !/^\d+$/.test(t) || !v1 || !/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(v1)) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(t)) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.`).update(rawBody).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(v1, "hex"), expected);
}
```

The receiver **stores each delivery before it answers**, so a crash after the `2xx` can't lose an event. The delivery's ID is the table's key, so a repeat changes nothing, and a separate worker handles the stored rows:

```ts title="receiver.mts"
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";
import { verifySignature } from "./verify-signature.mts";

const secret = process.env.MARFA_WEBHOOK_SECRET!;
const db = new DatabaseSync("deliveries.db");
db.exec(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deliveries (
  delivery_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, event_id TEXT, body TEXT NOT NULL, done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)`);
const storeWebhook = db.prepare("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO deliveries (delivery_id, event_id, body) VALUES (?, ?, ?)");

createServer((request, response) => {
  const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
  request.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => chunks.push(chunk));
  request.on("end", () => {
    const rawBody = Buffer.concat(chunks);
    const signature = request.headers["x-marfa-signature"];
    if (!verifySignature(rawBody, typeof signature === "string" ? signature : undefined, secret)) {
      response.writeHead(401).end();
      return;
    }
    const delivery = JSON.parse(rawBody.toString("utf8"));
    storeWebhook.run(delivery.delivery_id, delivery.event_id ?? null, rawBody.toString("utf8")); // a repeated webhook delivery changes nothing
    response.writeHead(204).end();
  });
}).listen(3000);
```

## Handle repeats and order

Answer webhooks with `2xx` **within 10 seconds**, so do slow work afterward. **Marfa promises neither order nor once:** an event can come twice with the same `delivery_id`, and a failed delivery waits for its retry while newer ones go through, so event 16 can arrive before 15. `event_id` is a decimal string that can pass 2^53: **compare it as a `BigInt`**.

- **A copy of the latest state** keeps the highest `event_id` applied for each item and ignores a lower one.
- **A worker that must act on every change** records the delivery as done in the same transaction as its effect, or makes the effect safe to repeat:

```ts title="worker.mts"
const todo = db.prepare("SELECT delivery_id, body FROM deliveries WHERE done = 0");
const finish = db.prepare("UPDATE deliveries SET done = 1 WHERE delivery_id = ?");

for (const row of todo.all() as { delivery_id: string; body: string }[]) {
  db.exec("BEGIN");
  effect(JSON.parse(row.body)); // writes to this database, or is safe to repeat
  finish.run(row.delivery_id);
  db.exec("COMMIT");
}
```

## Handle a failed webhook delivery

Marfa makes eight attempts at each delivery, trying again when your receiver can't be reached, is too slow, or answers `5xx`, `408` or `429`, and waiting longer when `Retry-After` asks. Any other `4xx`, or a redirect, ends it at once. A delivery Marfa gives up on is `failed`, and its record later expires. **A webhook whose every attempt has failed for a day appears in `marfa attention`** until an attempt succeeds, or you change its `url`, turn it off or delete it.

**A webhook's pending deliveries are capped** by the `webhook_backlog_deliveries` and `webhook_backlog_bytes` [settings](/reference/instance-settings#stored-settings): a new delivery past either is recorded `canceled` and never sent, while those already pending still go.

**The highest `event_id` you stored is no cursor:** if event 25 arrives while 22 waits for its retry, resuming after 25 skips 22. A receiver that must not miss a change keeps a cursor that only the [event stream](/build/keep-in-sync) advances, in order, and reads the stream after an outage. An `attention.raised` sent from memory has no `event_id` and can't be replayed ([the contract](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md#eventsattention-memory-body)).

[List webhook deliveries](/reference/api/webhooks/listWebhookDeliveries), or `marfa webhooks deliveries`, shows each one's `status` and your receiver's last answer. Once the fault is fixed, [redeliver](/reference/api/webhooks/redeliverWebhookDelivery) a `failed` delivery, with the same `delivery_id`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa webhooks redeliver <webhook-id> <delivery-id>
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /webhooks/<webhook-id>/deliveries/<delivery-id>/redeliver
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

Marfa answers `202`, or refuses `409 conflict` with a `details.reason`:

- **`webhook_inactive`:** the webhook is turned off.
- **`credential_unavailable`:** the webhook's key or app is no longer valid.
- **`delivery_not_failed`:** the delivery isn't `failed`.
- **`delivery_expired`:** the delivery record has expired.
- **`backlog_full`:** the webhook's pending deliveries are at their limit.

## Change what a webhook sends

[Update a webhook](/reference/api/webhooks/updateWebhook) to change its `url`, `events`, `type_filter` or `active`. A deleted webhook sends no pending deliveries.

The rules are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) chapter of the contract.
